question_text: How does one visualise DNA on an agarose gel?

insider_note: Two things: a dye and ultraviolet light. Both are needed — DNA stained but not lit shows nothing.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The stain
steps.margin_note: Name the stain and say what it binds to.
lines: The separated DNA fragments are stained with
Ethidium bromide slots itself between the base
steps.why: The dye binds only to DNA, so only the DNA bands will glow and the rest of the gel stays dark.
common_mistakes: Naming a different stain. It is ETHIDIUM BROMIDE.
Saying the DNA bands can be seen without staining. Unstained DNA cannot be seen at all — ethidium bromide is what makes the bands visible.
steps.memory_tip: One dye that sticks only to DNA.

steps.label: The light
steps.margin_note: The light, the colour, and why both steps are needed.

lines.text: Ethidium bromide plus UV light: orange bands

lines: The stained gel is then exposed to ULTRAVIOLET
The DNA appears as bright ORANGE coloured bands.
Without the UV light the stained DNA cannot be
steps.why: The dye fluoresces only under ultraviolet light, so the light is as necessary as the stain.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the UV light. Staining alone shows nothing.
Saying the bands are blue. They fluoresce ORANGE.
steps.memory_tip: Stain it, then shine ultraviolet on it.
